### 1. What's Life Like in This Ward?
In the summer, our tin and concrete roofs heat up like tavas, reaching over 34°C with zero officially recorded trees or parks to give us shade. When the rains arrive, even a small shower brings pani bharaav because almost 98% of our roads have no drains to carry water away. On top of that, 80% of our slum homes are not linked to sewer lines, so dirty water often overflows into the lanes where our children play.

---

### 2. Problems and What We Can Do About Them

| Problem | How Bad Is It? | Why Does This Happen Here? | What Can Be Done? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Street Flooding** | Terrible pani bharaav even after a light shower. | About 98.2% of our roads have no roadside drains at all. | Build simple side drains and clean out choking points so water moves quickly. |
| **Extreme Heat** | Roofs bake up to 34.3°C, turning rooms into ovens. | Most homes have plain tin or cement sheets that trap afternoon heat. | Paint rooftops with white heat-reflecting paint to keep indoor rooms cooler. |
| **No Trees or Shade** | The ward officially has 0 recorded parks and 0 trees. | Open spaces were built over rapidly without leaving soil for planting. | Plant local shade trees along wider gullies and in front of community halls. |
| **Dirty Water Overflow** | Stagnant, foul water sits near homes. | About 80% of slum homes are not connected to underground sewer lines. | Lay underground pipes and build covered naalas to carry wastewater safely away. |
| **Water Shortage** | Groundwater levels dip fast when peak heat begins. | Rainwater runs straight into the dirt and gets wasted instead of soaking down. | Put rooftop rainwater collection tanks on community buildings and let rainwater soak into the ground. |

---

### 3. How Will the Money, Workers and Time Be Used?

| Work To Be Done | How Many? | Money (Rs.) | Workers Needed | Time Needed | Who Is Responsible? |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| White heat-reflecting paint for rooftops | 15 building clusters | Rs. 1,800,000 | 30 workers | 1 month | PMC Building & Development Department |

**Summary:**
- **Total money being used:** Rs. 1,800,000 out of Rs. 5,000,000
- **Money left over:** Rs. 3,200,000
- **Workers needed:** 30 person-months
- **Everything done in:** 1 months

---

### 4. What Should the Ward Officer Do? (Step by Step)

1. **Week 1:** Visit Ganesh Nagar and Vadgaon Sheri slum pockets to select 15 tightly-packed building clusters with the hottest tin and concrete roofs.
2. **Week 2:** Purchase certified white heat-reflecting roof paint and bring together the 30 workers with rollers, brushes, and safety ladders.
3. **Week 3:** Wash and clean all selected rooftops thoroughly, then apply the first thick coat of white paint on every roof.
4. **Week 4:** Apply the second coat for complete sun protection, inspect the finish, and talk to residents to confirm the heat inside has dropped.

---

### 5. How Will Residents Know Things Are Getting Better?

- ✅ Homes with white-painted roofs should feel noticeably cooler in the afternoon, making it easier to rest inside.
- ✅ Families under these roofs will need to run their table fans much less, helping save on monthly power bills.
- ✅ The bright white rooftops will be clearly visible across the cluster, showing work was done right above their heads.
